To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the HTLV-1 virus can spread between cells through tunneling nanotubules and that the nucleoside drug cytarabine can inhibit this process.

(i) HTLV-1 infected cells are interconnected by TNTs, (ii) the HTLV-1 p8 protein induces the formation of TNTs, (iii) AraC reduces the number of TNTs, and (iv) AraC reduces HTLV-1 infection of target cells.
the human T-cell leukemia HTLV-1 is transmitted through tunneling nanotube (TNN) conduits and that cytarabine inhibits HTLV-1 infection and TNT formation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of TNTs in HTLV-1 infection and transmission and the possibility of targeting TNTs to inhibit viral transmission.
the development of new anti-HTLV- 1 drugs.
the role of the human T-cell leukemia viruses (HTLV- I and II), which are retroviruses endemic in the Caribbean and Japan.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HTLV-1 virus is highly dependent on cellular conduits, such as TNTs, to transmit the virus between cells and that the viral protein p8 promotes this mechanism of viral transmission.
cytarabine is able to inhibit TNT formation and HTLV-1 intercellular transmission.
cytarabine reduces the formation of tunneling nanotube structures and the transmission of human T cell leukemia virus type 2 (HTLV-2) between T lymphocytes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

cytarabine inhibits HTLV-1 cell-to-cell transmission and this inhibition is mediated through inhibition of TNT formation and that p8 induces TNT formation and that the nucleoside cytarabine can be used to inhibit TNT formation and cell-to-cell transmission of HTLV.
we found that HTLV- 1 expressing cells are connected through TNTs.
we have shown that HTLV-2 infected cells are interconnected by thin structures containing F actin and lack of microtubules connecting two cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HTLV-1 p8 protein increases viral transmission by inducing the formation of cellular conduits.
TNTs are a novel target for anti-HTLV- 1 therapy.
cytarabine could be used in HTLV-1 patients to reduce viral transmission and thus the risk of developing HTLV-1 associated diseases.
